method: Nine fresh ChatGPT Work executors (one per case and instruction set) received only the frozen selected guidance, the trigger and read-only synthetic inputs. A separate agent graded anonymized answers against the matching rubric. Effective model version, cost and execution time were not recorded. These were explicit-reference runs, not automatic skill discovery, full retro sweeps or production sessions.
interpretation: All nine central recommendations were correct. A grade counts a compound expected item only if all its clauses are present. The first comparison motivated an instruction edit. The final three replays use the same cases, so their scores include tuning on this sample.

expected: use the original PR or Learning-Id and replay R17 to retain stable retry keys for the observed disconnect case; treat the exported copy as the same episode
distinguish the two first-attempt workers in dispatch-33 from one worker retrying; keep the prior result and link the different cause to it
propose a prospective observable concurrency check with two workers on one order and one resulting job; keep the disconnect/retry control
negative_expected: strengthen transport retries as a fix for dispatch-33
count the support copy as an independent confirmation or claim a proposed concurrency fix already passed

expected: use the local PR and replay for the original scoped success despite the unavailable index; report limited coverage
leave the later mechanism and application of the loaded fix unresolved; request a discriminating trace of loaded revision, worker IDs and submission keys or an equivalent bounded check
retain the earlier prediction and observed result while leaving the new effect untested
negative_expected: treat an unavailable index as evidence that no attempt exists
infer a concurrency defect, prescribe a global retry change or count an unsuccessful application from the symptom alone

expected: retrieve proposal 44 and the original RL-8 comparison, identifying the recorded prediction and both outcomes under the earlier conditions
use the existing learning identity or original owner link and explicitly account for the earlier withdrawal in the current decision
preserve the benefit for a crashed worker and the counterexample for a silent live worker; propose a changed precondition or bounded check that can distinguish them before reconsidering
negative_expected: cite only a memory summary or miscount RL-9 as an independent confirmation
repeat the unchanged 20 s proposal, erase the earlier result, or claim a proposed alternative already passed

Keep the 60 s lease for live workers, as recorded in proposal 44. Verify the deployed setting first. The reported 40 s measures queue delay during deploys and does not establish the configured expiry.

Proposal 44 predicted that a 20 s lease would recover abandoned work sooner while preserving one delivery per upload. Replay RL-8 confirmed faster recovery after a crash. But a healthy worker also went silent during a 35 s upload. At 20 s, a second worker reclaimed the upload at 21 s and both delivered it. At 60 s, it was delivered once. That result led the maintainer to withdraw the proposal. RL-9 summarizes the same replay.

Reopen `retro-20260813-abandoned-claims` if the relay can establish that the old worker has surrendered ownership or can no longer deliver.
